result.instructions:
Tools for reverse engineering the program open in Ghidra. Call get_program_info first to confirm
which binary you are working on. Addresses are hex strings such as "0x401000". List tools are
paginated: pass offset/limit and check has_more. Prefer the address-based tools for modifications,
since function names can be ambiguous.

tool_schemas.name: get_program_info
tool_schemas.description:
Identify the target program: name, format, language/architecture, compiler spec,
        image base, address range, size, entry points, and hashes.

tool_schemas.name: list_functions
tool_schemas.description:
List functions (name and entry address), optionally filtered by a case-insensitive
        substring of the name.

tool_schemas.name: list_methods
tool_schemas.description: Deprecated: use list_functions. Lists function names only.

tool_schemas.name: search_functions_by_name
tool_schemas.description: Search for functions whose name contains the given substring (case-insensitive).

tool_schemas.name: list_classes
tool_schemas.description: List class namespaces (fully qualified names).

tool_schemas.name: list_namespaces
tool_schemas.description: List all non-global namespaces (fully qualified names).

tool_schemas.name: list_segments
tool_schemas.description: List memory blocks with address range, size, and permissions.

tool_schemas.name: list_imports
tool_schemas.description: List imported (external) symbols and their libraries.

tool_schemas.name: list_exports
tool_schemas.description: List exported symbols / entry points.

tool_schemas.name: list_data_items
tool_schemas.description: List defined data with address, label, type, and value.

tool_schemas.name: list_strings
tool_schemas.description:
List defined strings with their addresses, optionally filtered by a case-insensitive
        substring of the content.

tool_schemas.name: get_function_by_address
tool_schemas.description:
Get the function at or containing an address: name, signature, body range,
        calling convention.

tool_schemas.name: decompile_function
tool_schemas.description:
Decompile a function by name and return C pseudocode. Fails if the name is ambiguous;
        use decompile_function_by_address in that case.

tool_schemas.name: decompile_function_by_address
tool_schemas.description: Decompile the function at or containing an address and return C pseudocode.

tool_schemas.name: disassemble_function
tool_schemas.description:
Disassemble the instructions in a function's body (address, bytes, instruction,
        end-of-line comment).

tool_schemas.name: get_xrefs_to
tool_schemas.description: List references to an address, with the function each reference comes from.

tool_schemas.name: get_xrefs_from
tool_schemas.description: List references from a single instruction or data address.

tool_schemas.name: get_function_xrefs
tool_schemas.description: List references to a function's entry point, by name or (preferably) address.

tool_schemas.name: get_function_calls
tool_schemas.description:
Function-level call graph, one level deep. Callers are call sites that reach this
        function; callees are calls made from anywhere in its body, including indirect calls
        (direct=false). offset/limit apply to each list separately.

tool_schemas.name: read_memory
tool_schemas.description:
Read up to 4096 bytes of program memory as hex and ASCII. Unmapped or uninitialized
        bytes are shown as '??' and listed in `gaps`.

tool_schemas.name: rename_function_by_address
tool_schemas.description: Rename the function at or containing an address.

tool_schemas.name: rename_function
tool_schemas.description:
Rename a function by its current name. Fails if the name is ambiguous; prefer
        rename_function_by_address.

tool_schemas.name: rename_data
tool_schemas.description: Rename the label of defined data (or an existing symbol) at an address.

tool_schemas.name: rename_variable
tool_schemas.description:
Rename a local variable or parameter as shown in the decompiler. Identify the function
        by function_address (preferred) or function_name.

tool_schemas.name: set_function_prototype
tool_schemas.description: Set a function's signature from a C prototype, e.g. "int foo(char *buf, int len)".

tool_schemas.name: set_local_variable_type
tool_schemas.description: Set the data type of a decompiler variable, e.g. "char *", "DWORD", "MY_STRUCT *".

tool_schemas.name: set_decompiler_comment
tool_schemas.description:
Set the pre-comment at an address (shown in the decompiler). An empty comment clears
        it.

tool_schemas.name: set_disassembly_comment
tool_schemas.description:
Set the end-of-line comment at an address (shown in the disassembly). An empty comment
        clears it.

limitations: Ghidra and Temurin runtime were unpacked under /dev/shm because PJ1 persistent filesystem lacked enough free space. Current-run MCP success is confirmed; reboot-persistent application deployment is not.
The headless stdio MCP protocol initialize, tools/list (28 exact schemas), and one get_program_info read call succeeded. Eight project-mutating tools were advertised, not called.

Parent's separate gateway observation indicates automatic collection was disabled and no automatic report was sent; one explicitly requested one-off scan was accepted. Parent evidence itself was not directly read by this subtask.
No harness natural-language model turn, Gateway MCP registry approval, Gateway tool call, or registry change was tested/performed.
No real or untrusted binary was analyzed; only the generated ELF fixture was imported/analyzed and it was never executed.
The process was unconfined under AppArmor and ran as UID 1000 with that user's ordinary filesystem access. No account separation or sandbox property is claimed.

The bridge listener was observed on mapped IPv4 loopback during the hold. The parent independently reported no process/listener after shutdown. Local bridge authentication is not demonstrated; Origin/Host behavior is not authentication.
HTTP/SSE MCP modes, GUI, remote network access, project persistence, write tools, arbitrary user binaries, and post-reboot startup were not exercised.
